output.title: Outbox and saga checkout
output.description: A transactional outbox publishes order events; a saga orchestrates inventory and payment, compensating when a step fails.

simulations.title: Twenty checkouts, happy path
simulations.description: Each order commits with its outbox row, then the saga reserves stock, charges the card and confirms.

action.text: The order row and its OrderCreated event commit in one database transaction. No dual write, so no lost events.
The outbox relay tails the write-ahead log and publishes each outbox row to Kafka.
The saga runs one step at a time: reserve stock, charge the card, then confirm the order. Every step is saved, so a restart resumes where it left off.
OrderConfirmed goes out through the same outbox, and the customer gets a receipt.

simulations.title: Declines and flaky payments
simulations.description: Transient payment errors are retried with the same idempotency key; a fraud rule declines cards for three seconds and the saga compensates.

action.text: One payment call in five times out. The consumer retries in place with the same Idempotency-Key, so a retry never charges twice.
A fraud rule starts declining every card. The saga compensates: it releases the reserved stock, then cancels the order.
The rule is rolled back. Every customer still hears back: a receipt or a cancellation.
